Chairman’s Address Corporate 
Overview 01
Are We Ready?
“India has the talent, the English 
advantage, and the policy 
momentum. We have no excuse 
not to lead.”The world has changed. Not gradually. It has changed the way tectonic plates shift — suddenly, 
irreversibly, and in a way that leaves nothing quite as it was before.
Everywhere I go today, people are talking about Artificial Intelligence. I have experienced firsthand 
what AI can do. It is predicting equipment failures before they happen, compressing weeks of 
geological analysis into hours, designing drug molecules in days that once took researchers years, 
and teaching children in ways personalised to each student's pace. The scale of what AI is doing — 
right now, across every sector, in every country — is unlike anything I have seen in fifty years of 
business. This is not the future. This is now.Dear Shareholders,
I am more optimistic about India today than I 
have ever been. We have the talent. We have the 
English language advantage that no other large 
nation in the world can match. We have a young, 
technology-adept population. Look at what the 
US has done with AI. From frontier model 
development at OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and 
Anthropic, to the physical infrastructure — the 
data centres, the chips, the energy grids, the 
whole game has changed. And now, the world's 
largest technology companies are looking 
towards India. Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta have announced over $100 billion in data 
centre investments across Asia, with India as a 
premier destination. They are coming for our 
talent, our energy capacity, and our digital 
infrastructure. Most importantly, they are 
coming because the future of AI runs through 
fibre — and India is laying it fast.
Without fibre, there is no AI. Every prompt you 
type, every image generated, every business 
decision an algorithm informs — it travels 
through glass threads thinner than a human hair, 
at the speed of light. The global hyperscalers are 
spending hundreds of billions building this 
infrastructure, and they need partners like India 
— young engineers, growing energy capacity, an 
expanding fibre grid. Every AI model trained, 
every transaction processed, travels through 
fibre optic cable. This is the central nervous 
system of the digital economy. And India is 
building it at scale.
I left Patna at nineteen with a set of dreams and 
have spent decades watching this country inch 
toward its destiny. It is now sprinting. This is India's best time and opportunity.
AI saves me 75% of my time. I use it every day 
— to ask sharper questions, to cut through 
complexity, to arrive at decisions faster. If it 
changes how I work, imagine what it does for 
1.4 billion people — engineers, doctors, farmers, 
teachers, entrepreneurs — all connected 
through a fibre network that reaches every 
corner of the country. India's digital economy is 
already growing faster than almost any other in 
the world. Our start-up ecosystem is the third 
largest on the planet. UPI processes more 
transactions in a month than most countries do 
in a year. This is what happens when you 
combine fibre, AI, and the ambition of a 
billion-plus people.People sometimes ask me why I think in such a long time horizon. 500 years is an unusual number but the 
right number. When you build for 500 years, you think differently. You do not treat technology as a trend to 
be followed — you treat it as a foundation to be built.
The investments being made today in fibre, data centres, AI research, and skilling millions of young Indians 
are the foundations of a civilisation-level leap. Use AI for entrepreneurship. Use it to build ideas and 
strategies. That is how we create jobs at scale, eradicate poverty, and fulfil the Prime Minister's dream of a 
Viksit Bharat — not through incremental improvement, but through exponential leverage.
At STL, we have spent thirty years believing that human progress moves at the speed at which we share 
ideas. In FY26, we launched Neuralis — a connectivity suite purpose-built for AI data centres — and 
introduced India's first Hollow Core Fibre cable, achieving 46% faster transmission and near-zero latency. In 
the UK, our 4-core Multi-Core Fibre cable expanded data capacity per strand. In the US, our Lugoff facility 
positioned STL as a primary partner for critical digital infrastructure. We have moved next-generation fibre 
out of our laboratories and into active customer pilots. We have not waited for the future. We have 
gone to meet it.
But progress must be purposeful. This year we commissioned Maharashtra's 
first green hydrogen plant in optical manufacturing, abated 6,348 
tCO2 of carbon emissions, and diverted 59% of manufacturing waste into 
industrial by-products. We have transformed 4.78 million lives, nurtured 4 
lakh trees, and replenished 2.69 million cubic metres of water. Our 
Jeewan Jyoti initiative has empowered over 30,000 women toward 
financial dignity.
 
We are fibering the world at AI scale — with 
speed and with conscience.
To every team member, every entrepreneur, 
every young Indian building this 
future — you are the real 
story. The raw material of the 
future is connectivity and 
India has it. 
And we are only just 
beginning.
The results, 
I assure you, will be 
phenomenal.Building the Neural 
Networks of the AI AgeBuilding for 500 Years
This Is India's Moment
Fibre Is the Foundation of Everything
Anil 
Agarwal

Chairman, STL

Sterlite Technologies Limited Corporate 
Overview Letter to the Shareholders
at AI Scale
In October 2025, Google DeepMind's WeatherNext AI predicted Hurricane Melissa's Category 5 landfall in 
Jamaica a full seven days before it struck — enough time for authorities to evacuate coastal communities. 
Behind that prediction were thousands of servers processing satellite feeds and ocean data simultaneously, 
in real time. 
AI got the credit. The fibre carried the data that made this possible. It is doing the heavy lifting no one sees, 
turning computational potential into human reality.
Quietly. Instantly. At a scale that was unimaginable a decade ago.
If FY25 was the year we asked, "Are networks ready for AI?", FY26 was the year we received our answer. AI is 
no longer approaching. It has arrived, and it has brought with it a set of demands that make last year's 
infrastructure benchmarks feel quaint.
Consider what has changed in just one year. AI model sizes are doubling every 18 months, and the data center 
power densities required to train them have crossed thresholds that traditional facilities simply weren't built to 
handle. The largest AI models being trained today consume compute clusters running tens of thousands of 
GPUs — simultaneously. At the same time, AI inference is moving rapidly to the edge—into our factories, our 
offices, our hospitals, and our smart city grids. The data centre is no longer a single building; it is a distributed 
organism that breathes through fibre. It has become load-bearing infrastructure for modern civilization. If the 
fiber layer fails to scale, the entire AI revolution stalls.Density is the new distance 
For three decades, fibre was measured in kilometres — 
how far you could carry a signal. Today, the metrics is 
how dense you can get inside a single rack. Inside the 
data center, GPU trays and server racks require 
unprecedented fibre counts to prevent bottlenecks. 
"Fibre-to-the-device" is no longer a concept, it is an 
immediate design requirement.There are three realities defining us right now:
Fibre is becoming intelligent
Fibre is no longer ‘passive’. We are 
moving toward adaptive routing and 
optical sensing—fiber that can detect 
physical stress, temperature shifts, or 
intrusions.  As AI consumes more of 
the network, the network itself is 
beginning to report back.
Speed of deployment as a variable 
AI infrastructure investment cycles are moving faster than traditional telecom build cycles. 
Hyperscalers are commissioning data centres on 18-month timelines. Network operators connecting 
rural communities under programmes like BharatNet cannot afford multi-year deployment windows. 
Scaling at AI speed requires modular, pre-connectorized, plug-and-play solutions that allow operators 
to build out networks in weeks rather than months. And STL has been building toward it for years.It is very easy to treat this as a capacity story — lay more fibre, move more data, done. But that misses what 
is actually happening on the ground, inside the data centres and edge deployments we are building with 
our customers.
—and So Have the StakesActually Means
Last year we asked whether networks could 
keep up. This year, the question is sharper: can 
fibre be deployed fast enough, dense 
enough, and smart enough to match the 
velocity of AI itself? That is the question that 
defined our business in FY26.

From Foundation to Scale
Our thirty-year journey as an agile partner in global digital infrastructure has evolved.We weathered 
downturns, restructured where we had to, and made a deliberate choice to move beyond our origins 
as a telecom infrastructure business toward something more ambitious: a global AI connectivity and 
digital infrastructure company. That transition wasn't linear. We sharpened our focus, expanded our 
footprint across the US, Europe, India, and China, and built our capabilities around what AI-era 
networks actually demand.
Moving beyond traditional gigabit connectivity, our integrated approach in FY26 focused on tackling 
the severe physical constraints of modern networks, co-crafting ultra-dense optical solutions that 
extend network lifespans while maintaining reliability under unprecedented data loads. We sharpened 
our focus on what we do best: end-to-end optical solutions, from the glass we draw to the gigabit 
connections at the edge. We made difficult calls on cost structure. We deepened relationships with 
customers who were themselves navigating an infrastructure landscape being redrawn by AI. 
We moved next-generation technologies like Multi-Core and Hollow-Core fibre out of our laboratories 
and into active customer pilots, while simultaneously securing critical US Plenum qualifications to 
unlock high-density enterprise and Data Center environments. By prioritizing operational discipline 
alongside  product innovation, we built the foundation required to sustain long-term growth.Sterlite Technologies Limited
FY26 was a year of execution. Global demand for fibre and optical connectivity continued to outpace supply 
in several categories. Geopolitical factors, including supply chain restructuring and localisation mandates in 
key markets, created both disruption and opportunity. We navigated both gracefully and with intent.Highlights
Accelerating innovation - By integrating glass science with precision manufacturing, STL is co-creating 
advanced high-density, low-latency solutions. One of the major milestone was the launch of Neuralis, a 
purpose-built connectivity suite for AI data centres. Alongside it, we introduced India's first Hollow Core 
Fibre (HCF) cable — an air-core architecture that achieves ~46% faster transmission and near-zero latency. In 
the UK, our 4-core Multi-Core Fibre Unitube cable significantly expanded data capacity per strand, 
addressing the bandwidth demands of next-generation networks. For deployment efficiency, CONCAT — our 
pre-connectorised, plug-and-play solution — is reducing on-site labour and cutting installation timelines for 
operators. And in the US, the expansion of our IBR portfolio to higher fibre counts is enabling the kind of 
rapid network scaling that broadband and AI infrastructure programmes now require.Expanding global footprints with customer centricity - We established partnerships with Colt, Netomnia, 
Mynet, SLICFiber, and Swoop — operators building long-horizon infrastructure across markets that matter. 
Across North America, the United Kingdom, Europe, and Asia, the momentum was tangible longer-term, 
more technically deep, and increasingly centred on co-developing solutions. 
Deepening Our US Presence - With our Lugoff Manufacturing facility, we are fully ready 
to support the US market, capitalizing on reshoring tailwinds to position STL as a 
primary partner for regional broadband and Data Center expansion.We are building for what comes next - We are growing our capability through our R&D centres, through 
academic partnerships, and through hiring. We are investing in people who understand how to fiberise an AI 
cluster at scale. 
Thirty years ago, STL began with a simple belief in the transformative power of connectivity. uman progress 
would always rely on the speed at which we share ideas.Thirty years in, that core conviction hasn't changed. 
We are weaving the nervous system of the future. 
Thank you for your continued trust and partnership as we build an infrastructure that matters.
Pravin Agarwal

Optical Networking Business
A Year of 
For years, STL had been building quietly — laying fiber, expanding capacity, deepening glass technology, 
getting closer to the growth markets. FY26 was the year where STL’s core strength being built over many years 
came to play to support the global AI data Center infrastructure build globally.
The AI-led network build-out from hyperscalers in North America, operators in Europe, and infrastructure 
builders across Asia were all looking for solutions both at speed and at scale. And STL had built a fully 
integrated, Glass-to-Data Centres connectivity manufacturing ecosystem designed to eliminate deployment 
risk, optimise duct utilisation, and reduce field installation time from day one. By engineering high-density 
ribbon architectures like Celesta IBR and blow-optimised portfolios like MicroLite HD, STL addresses the critical 
pain points of duct congestion, skilled labour shortages, and rapid network monetisation. STL delivers 
commercially deployable, future-ready solution stacks that seamlessly balance extreme data centre and 
fibre-to-the-home densification with operational sustainability and long-term network longevity. 
In FY26, STL shipped its first Hyperscale High Fibre Count 6912 Indoor/Outdoor cable — a feat achieved in a 
short span of time, highlighting the agility and strengths of STL R&D team beating global benchmarks on 
turnaround times.
In North America, hyperscalers began deploying STL's 432F and 864F 200-micron microcables across their 
networks. And with the 1728F 200-micron IBR — one of the world's smallest diameter ribbons — STL set a new 
global record for jetting distance. 
The pivotal moment of FY26 arrived in June 2025 with the expansion of the Data Center Business portfolio and 
launch of Neuralis. A specialised product portfolio was launched.The story of FY26 ended the way every great 
year should — with momentum that carries straight into the next one.
From flame-retardant cable qualifications to precision-engineered high-density connectors, every product 
development decision made during the year had the same north star — build the physical backbone that AI 
infrastructure demands.Our Businesses
Optical Connectivity
FY26 has been a landmark year of growth and transformation, marked by significant milestones that have 
redefined our global footprint and strengthened our core capabilities. Across our Optical Fiber, Optical 
Fiber Cable, Optical Connectivity, Data Centres, and Enterprise businesses, we have transitioned from 
providing technology to building the very fabric of a digital-first world.
Through our "Connectivity on Wheels" demo van in the UK and Europe, we travelled across multiple 
regions, bringing our plug-and-play solutions directly to our customers. This commitment to local 
requirements was mirrored in our partnership with Wyre to accelerate fiber deployments and our 
collaboration with Mynet in Italy. For their Intacture project—a €50.2 million data centre built into the 
mountains of Trentino—we provided the optical fiber foundations for a facility led by the University of 
Trento and backed by the PNRR.In the Enterprise sector, we proved that connectivity can be both high-performing and high-purpose. In 
Italy, we showcased our integrated solutions designed to modernize rail networks, while our collaboration 
with SLIC Fiber in New York saw the launch of #FiberOfHope. This custom-engineered pink drop cable 
stood tall as a sign of hope and support to cancer patients. This spirit of partnership also flourished in 
our work with Wyre, where we co-engineered customized solutions to fast-track fiber-to-the-home 
deployments.
The year also marked a significant leap forward for our Data Centre business. We launched a dedicated 
DC portfolio, Introduced India’s first Hollow Core Fibre cable, enabling ~46% faster transmission and 
ultra-low latency through air-core fibre and expanded our IBR portfolio with 1728F 
and a DC-specific 3456F & 6912F high-count variants. By continuing to develop our very small form 
factor (VSFF) connector termination capabilities, we are well positioned to play a leading role in the 
AI-driven fiber infrastructure revolution.
The FY26 was the year we stepped forward, simplified complexity for our 
customers and brought the future into sharper focus

Management Discussion and Analysis
Navigating a
In FY 26, the world has outgrown the comfort of predictable patterns. The past year has delivered a series of 
tectonic structural shifts, forcing the global economy to transition from an era of frictionless globalization 
into a high-stakes landscape defined by intense geopolitical realignments, territorial conflicts, and 
paradigm-shifting inventions. On one hand, regional wars and vital maritime chokepoint vulnerabilities, such 
as the severe transit disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz have introduced energy volatility and persistent 
inflationary pressures that force central banks to keep capital tight. This friction is further accelerated by 
trade fragmentation and aggressive tariff walls, ending the classic, highly vulnerable "hub-and-spoke" model 
of international dependency. Yet, this geopolitical pressure cooker has simultaneously triggered an 
unprecedented wave of human ingenuity. We are witnessing an explosion of transformative inventions:generativeAI, has catalyzed one of the fastest global technology diffusion curves in human 
history, transitioning from a conversational novelty into one of the key foundational shifts of 
the modern economy. 
A McKinsey Analysis reported that by end of  2025, roughly 88% of organizations globally 
will utilize AI in at least one business function,up from just 55% two years prior, with 
enterprise adopters realizing an average 3.7x financial return for every dollar invested 
alongside average productivity gains of over 22%.
The most prominent theme that has defined the world & the industry 
we operate in over the past couple of years is Artificial Intelligence 
(AI). Since ChatGPT’s historic launch in late 2022, AI, especially

The ripple effects of the AI boom have been transformational on the global optical market. The 
fibre networking landscape is undergoing a massive demand growth driven by divergent 
customer needs across hyperscalers, telecommunications operators, and enterprise environments. 
AI clusters require ultra-high bandwidth, low latency, and extreme fiber density to support parallel 
processing. This shifting requirement is fundamentally altering the optical supply-demand balance 
and transitioning infrastructure inside server racks from copper to fiber. 
The rapid expansion of Generative AI is driving a shift from legacy Central Processing Unit (CPU) 
infrastructures to advanced Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) architectures. While traditional CPUs 
are designed to execute computing tasks sequentially, GPUs process thousands of data threads The Optical Supply-Demand Paradigm Shift:2. Market Overview for the

deploying Large Language Models (LLMs). To achieve the necessary computational scale, 
individual GPUs are interconnected into dense topologies called GPU Clusters, which effectively 
operate as a single, massive distributed supercomputer. 
This architecture fundamentally changes how data moves within a facility. Standard data centre 
workloads are historically "North-South" (data moving externally between users and servers). 
Conversely, AI workloads generate massive "East-West" traffic (data moving internally between 
servers). During AI model training, thousands of GPU nodes must continuously synchronize 
billions of data parameters with one another. Management Discussion and Analysis

An all-to-all connection indicates the irreplaceable requirement of optical fibre in AI datacentres and reflects 
sustained macroeconomic tailwinds and long-term structural infrastructure requirements.
Furthermore, satisfying the physical constraints of extreme bandwidth acceleration and stringent 
low-latency requirements across these multi-site architectures necessitates a transition toward specialized, 
next-generation fibre mediums designed to overcome standard silica-core performance boundaries:
Multi-Core Fiber (MCF) contains multiple independent data cores within a single optical fibre strand. It 
enables 4x–7x higher data capacity compared to standard single-core fibre. By maintaining the same 
physical size, it offers excellent space efficiency and reduces deployment and infrastructure costs. This 
technology is ideal for AI-driven data centres, long-haul 5G networks, and high-performance 
interconnects.Multicore Fiber: 
Light travels mainly through an air-filled core instead of solid silica, offering ~30–47% lower latency. 
Furthermore, it uses a broader spectrum, supporting very high-band signals from 800G to 1.6T and 
beyond.Hollow-Core Fiber:

CDMA (2G/3G)5G/6G led optical fibre densificationThe ongoing expansion of 5G and the initial preparations for 6G are driving a significant surge in demand 
for optical fiber and fiber optic cables.
Unlike previous mobile network generations, 5G relies on a highly dense architecture to achieve faster 
speeds, lower latency, and handle massive amounts of data. To make this work, especially in dense, urban 
areas, telecom operators must install numerous small cells, additional macro sites, and more antenna 
arrays. Every single one of these connection points requires high-capacity optical fiber for both backhaul 
and fronthaul networking, making fiber absolutely critical to current and future infrastructure upgrades.

Risk Management
We have established a risk management framework to identify, assess, manage, and monitor the key risks 
that could impact on the achievement of a company’s strategic, financial, operational, and compliance 
objectives. The Company’s risk management efforts are overseen by a dedicated Risk Management 
Committee supported by multi-tier structure to enable effective governance. By embedding risk thinking 
into decision-making, Risk management supports resilient growth, drives performance, and strengthens the 
organization's ability to navigate uncertainty with confidence. Apart from Risk management committee, 
Audit committee provides additional oversight through independent review and examination of the entire 
risk framework. Adequacy of Internal Controls.
The Company has a comprehensive framework for Internal Financial Controls (IFC) that integrates internal 
audit, enterprise risk management and compliance monitoring. The internal control environment is
supported by an independent Assurance Department complemented by outsourced audit teams. In line with 
its oversight responsibilities, the Audit Committee annually approves a risk-based Internal Audit Plan, which 
covers internal controls and risks across geographies, factories, offices, warehouses and centrally managed 
businesses and functions. Each quarter, the Audit Committee reviews significant audit observations, 
together with the status of remediation actions. . The Assurance function provides independent and 
objective assurance to Management and the Board on the adequacy and effectiveness of the Company’s
risk management and internal control systems, with the use of data and analytics further enhancing audit 
coverage and efficiency.The Company’s IFC framework is designed in accordance with the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations 
(COSO) principles and is commensurate with the scale and complexity of operations, meeting the 
requirements of the Act. The Management, together with the Statutory and Internal Auditors, undertakes 
regular testing of the control environment to assess design effectiveness and operating effectiveness.

Given the global scope and scale of STL’s operations, maintaining a seamless supply chain is crucial, as 
disruptions in manufacturing, delivery, logistics, or supply chain processes can adversely affect revenue and 
reputation.
Additionally, significant fluctuations in customer order timing and placement can impact planning and 
fulfilment. Risks are also associated with reliance on a single or limited source for certain input materials, 
while global shifts continue to impact the availability of rare earth materials.
The Company has implemented digital tools for scenario-based planning and forecasting to address these 
challenges. Furthermore, to guard against disruptions and volatility in global supply chains, STL is focusing 
on developing its vendor ecosystem, diversifying sourcing geographies, and emphasising local sourcing 
wherever possible.Risk Management
Geo-political and
STL operates in a dynamic global environment and is inherently exposed to various macroeconomic and 
geopolitical risks. These include general economic conditions, political uncertainties such as wars and 
conflicts, and local business risks across the countries where the Company operates. Regulatory factors, 
including changes in laws, trade regulations, and protectionist measures (such as reciprocal tariffs and 
anti-dumping duties), can affect the demand for STL’s offerings and impact overall competitiveness. In 
addition, volatility in commodity prices may directly or indirectly influence STL’s operational and financial 
performance.
The Company maintains a vigilant approach by continuously monitoring global developments and 
proactively implementing measures to mitigate potential adverse impacts. Foreign exchange volatility 
arising from geopolitical uncertainty is managed through a well-defined hedging policy.Operational
Operational risks are those that can negatively impact the Company’s operations. These risks relate to 
people, policies, procedures, and IT systems affecting product and service delivery to customers.
The Company has a strong mechanism in place to review operations, including business processes and 
procedures, to minimise risks relating to product and service delivery.

Strategic risks are those that are inherent to the industry in which the Company operates. These risks are 
analysed and mitigated through strategic actions on markets and customer offerings, investments in R&D 
and product innovation, among others. STL periodically assesses strategic risks related to the successful 
execution of its strategy, their impact on financial performance, the effectiveness of organisational 
structures and processes, and the retention and development of high-performing talent and leadership.

Risk Management
Cyber security remains a major risk due to the increasing sophistication of cyber threats. Incidents can involve 
data theft, ransomware attacks (resulting in financial or reputational losses), business interruptions caused by 
malware, phishing attacks, data privacy breaches, and IT system availability issues.
STL has adopted a defence-in-depth strategy to manage and mitigate these risks. The Company continues to 
evaluate evolving threats and invest in strengthening its security architecture and cyber security capabilities.
Financial risks encompass exposure to currency fluctuations, interest rates, credit, liquidity, taxation issues, 
and the ability to manage financial costs and optimise investment returns.
Additionally, there is a risk of errors in the Company’s financial reporting, such as the incorrect application of 
accounting principles, which could misrepresent its financial position.Cyber security risk
Ineffective internal controls over financial 
reporting may result in an unclear view of the 
Company’s financial position and business 
performance.
The Company maintains robust Internal 
Financial Controls (IFC) to ensure reporting is 
complete, transparent, and free from material 
weaknesses. Regular internal audits, conducted 
by independent external audit firms, ensure 
that controls are appropriately designed and 
operating effectively.Liquidity risksFinancial and
Financial reporting risk
The Company requires funds for both short-term 
operational needs and long-term investment projects, 
particularly growth initiatives.
To minimise risk, the Company aims to generate 
sufficient cash flows from ongoing operations. Along 
with available cash, cash equivalents, liquid 
investments, and committed funding facilities, this 
approach helps ensure liquidity in both the short and 
long term.
The Company manages liquidity risk by maintaining a 
balanced mix of long-term and short-term debt.Liquidity risks
The Company is exposed to fluctuations in the 
prices of raw materials and energy resources.
Strong policies and systems are in place to 
minimise raw material price risks to a large 
extent. The Company is vertically integrated 
globally, ensuring limited exposure to and 
impact from fluctuations in any single raw 
material.Commodity risks
The Company is exposed to counterparty risks 
relating to receivables and investments. It has 
clearly defined policies to mitigate these risks.
Limits are established for exposure to individual 
customers, and such exposure is closely 
monitored on an ongoing basis. Moreover, given 
the diverse nature of the Company’s businesses, 
trade receivables are spread across several 
customers, resulting in no significant 
concentration of credit risk.
Cash and liquid investments are held primarily in 
debt mutual funds and banks with high credit 
ratings approved by CRISIL. Priority is given to 
the security and liquidity of investments.Counterparty risksThe Company’s policy is to hedge all long-term 
foreign exchange risks and short-term exposures 
within defined parameters.
Long-term foreign exchange liabilities are fully 
hedged and held to maturity. The Company faces 
two major types of foreign currency risks: 
operational risks (such as purchasing or selling in 
foreign currencies) and borrowing risks 
denominated in foreign currencies.
The Company has an established and effective 
policy to manage both types of risks, which is 
regularly reviewed in response to significant 
economic and global developments.Foreign currency risks Interest Rate Risks
The Company is exposed to the risk of interest rate 
fluctuations in both domestic and foreign-currency 
borrowings.
It uses a prudent mix of Indian and foreign-currency 
borrowings within stipulated parameters to mitigate 
interest rate risk. This also helps achieve a lower 
blended interest rate.
Interest rates for Indian currency (rupee) 
borrowings are largely linked to the Marginal Cost 
of Funds-based Lending Rate (MCLR), while 
foreign-currency borrowings are linked to the 
Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR).

Risk Management
Compliance risks arise from violations of, or non-compliance with, applicable laws, 
regulations, and the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, all of which can 
significantly impact the Company’s financial, organisational, and reputational 
standing.
Adherence to laws and regulations is a fundamental aspect of STL’s Code of Business 
Conduct.
The Company has a strong compliance management framework, which includes 
mandatory e-learning programmes on the Code of Conduct, Prevention of Sexual 
Harassment (POSH), among others.
Further, a robust whistle-blower mechanism facilitates reporting of instances of 
non-compliance. In addition, independent external and internal auditors review the 
compliance management framework, including its operating effectiveness, and 
submit their findings to the Audit Committee.
This involves identifying and evaluating possible responses to risks, 
including assessing options in relation to risk appetite (accepting, 
mitigating, or transferring risks), the cost-benefit of potential 
responses, and the extent to which a response will reduce impact 
and/or likelihood.
Once mitigation plans are finalised, owners are identified and 
assigned responsibilities for implementation.This includes assessing risks based on their likelihood of occurrence 
and potential impact. Risks are assessed on both an inherent basis 
(gross risk without considering controls) and a residual basis (net 
risk after considering controls).
Residual risks are considered when prioritising monitoring and 
response activities.
The risk management process includes risk identification, assessment, response, 
monitoring, and reporting activities.
The foundational step in STL’s Enterprise Risk Management process. It involves 
systematically identifying internal and external events that could potentially 
impact the achievement of the Company’s objectives. STL actively scans its 
operating environment to detect emerging and existing risks across various 
dimensions. Once identified, risks are categorised into key groups: geopolitical 
and macroeconomic, strategic, operational, financial and reporting, and 
compliance.The Risk Committee reviews the adequacy and effectiveness of risk 
response plans and reports to the Board.
The Committee also monitors and reports on factors affecting identified 
risks, such as changes in business processes, operating and regulatory 
environments, and emerging trends.
These reviews aim to continuously strengthen the organisation’s risk 
management culture.

Purpose of 
The STL Foundation was built on a simple but powerful belief — that the same innovation driving the world's 
digital revolution can and must be turned toward its most pressing human challenges. We design scalable, 
technology-powered solutions that open doors to education, strengthen healthcare systems, accelerate 
women's empowerment, and protect our environment. Aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, 
we don't just measure our impact in numbers — we measure it in futures unlocked, barriers broken, and 
communities that dare to dream bigger than before.
Story Behind  
In 2012, Mr. Pravin Agarwal, Vice Chairman of STL, established the STL Foundation with the belief that 
technology, when placed in the hands of communities, does not just improve lives. It transforms them. The 
Foundation began as a registered public charitable trust. A symbolic corpus. And a conviction that the same 
innovation driving STL's business could be turned toward something far more fundamental — people. More 
than a decade later, that belief has grown into a strategic, impact-driven platform anchored in STL's deepest 
purpose:
Transforming billions of lives by connecting the world.
The STL Foundation exists to make that promise real — one programme, one community, one life at a time.Ms. Shweta Agarwal

something that creates real, lasting change.

for All
Our Swasthya Suraksha Program is a flagship healthcare initiative dedicated to delivering primary 
healthcare, preventive awareness, and behavioural change interventions to India’s most underserved tribal 
and rural communities. Through a community-led, technology-enabled approach, the Program reaches 
marginalised geographies with a strong focus on tribal women and children. In FY 2025-26, AI-enabled 
diagnostic services were deployed at camp level, improving early detection of anaemia, malnutrition, and 
communicable diseases. The Program received the Indian Social Impact Awards 2025.Swasthya Suraksha Program
86 Thousand+ 
lives benefited in FY26
10% reduction in anaemia prevalence in the project area27,000+ 
teleconsultations conducted2.7 Million+

SDG Linkage: SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, SDG 10: 
Reduced Inequalities, SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals by 
strengthening access to primary healthcare and preventive 
health services in underserved geographies. Anaemia among women in tribal communities of 
Gadchiroli & Nandurbar had long been a silent health 
crisis - widespread, underdiagnosed, and largely 
untreated. Through the Swasthya Suraksha Program, 
a structured four-month intervention cycle was 
designed to address this gap systematically. 
The process begins with detection. In the first month, 
women are screened at health camps across villages 
in the project area. Those identified with low 
haemoglobin levels are enrolled into the intervention 
- receiving iron and nutritional supplements along 
with personalised dietary guidance from trained 
health workers.
Over the following three months, health workers 
maintain continuous contact with each enrolled 
woman - tracking supplement adherence, reinforcing 
dietary habits, and conducting regular follow-up 
visits. Progress is measured against each woman's 
individual baseline health data. Where improvement is recorded at the four-month mark, the outcome is
 reported. Where it is not, the intervention continues 
until recovery is confirmed.
This cycle runs throughout the year, reaching women 
from different villages and locations across the 
project area - ensuring the Program is not a one-time 
event but a sustained, community-embedded health 
intervention.
At the close of FY 2025-26, the cumulative impact of 
these individual intervention cycles was reflected in a 
single, significant outcome: a 10% reduction in 
anaemia prevalence among women across the 
project area, measured against baseline data.
This result demonstrates what becomes possible 
when detection, supplementation, dietary guidance, 
and continuous follow-through are delivered together 
- consistently, across communities, and throughout 
the year.Impact Story:
Turning the Tide on Anaemia
Every improvement is earned through months of consistent care - detection, 
supplementation, guidance, and follow-through.

ANALYSIS REPORTSTL is a trusted name in the industry with a strong 
global presence spanning three continents and 
serving customers across 100 countries. Our expert 
offerings in Optical cable, Optical Connectivity, Data 
Centres, and Digital and Technology solutions have 
won us the trust of leading names in telecom, cloud, 
and large enterprises.
In the US, STL’s fibre optic and connectivity 
solutions are helping the country build ubiquitous 
broadband networks. STL has strengthened its 
presence with an advanced manufacturing facility in 
South Carolina. In the UK, STL has been front and 
centre of the UK’s digital transformation journey for 
over 10 years.  We are serving the optical and 
network build needs of our UK-based customers 
with design innovation and co-creation and shorter 
lead times.
In Europe, STL is driving design innovation in the 
optical network space to support national 
connectivity programs and help build ubiquitous 
broadband, FTTx, and 5G networks. Through its 
advanced Optical Fibre cable (OFC) and Optical 
Connectivity facilities in Italy, STL has helped in 
meeting the fibre demand and expedited fibre 
rollouts across the European region. The company’s 
optical solutions are helping accelerate 5G 
connectivity and smart living in the Middle East, and 
are driving digital inclusion in Africa. STL integrates 
R&D and product development for the region. STL 
started its journey in Australia in 2020 when it 
became the trusted optical partner for the second 
largest telecom operator in Australia. Since then, it 
has been an integral part of the region’s digital 
transformation journey.
STL has also completed 15 years of operations in 
Haimen, China. To date, our China plant has filed 84 
patents and been granted 69 certificates, including 
19 invention patents.

INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS
The Company has in place adequate internal 
financial controls commensurate with the size, 
scale and complexity of its operations. During the 
year, such controls were tested and the Company 
has, in all material respects, maintained adequate 
internal financial controls over financial reporting 
as of March 31, 2026 and is operating effectively. 
The Board has devised systems, policies and 
procedures/ frameworks, which are currently 
operational within the Company for ensuring the 
orderly and efficient conduct of its business, which 
includes adherence to Company’s policies, 
safeguarding assets of the Company, prevention and detection of frauds and errors, accuracy and 
completeness of the accounting records and timely 
preparation of reliable financial information. In line 
with best practices, the Audit Committee and the 
Board reviews these internal controls to ensure 
they remain effective and are designed to achieve 
their intended purpose. Where weaknesses, if any, 
are identified as a result of the reviews, corrective 
and preventive actions are then put in place to 
strengthen controls. 
The systems/ frameworks include proper 
delegation of authority, operating philosophies, 
policies and procedures, effective IT systems 
aligned to business requirements, an internal audit 
framework, an ethics framework, a risk 
management framework and adequate segregation 
of duties to ensure an acceptable level of risk. 
The Company has documented Standard Operating 
Procedures (‘SOP’) for key functions such as for 
procurement, project/ expansion management, 
capital expenditure, human resources, sales and 
marketing, finance, treasury, compliance 
management, safety, health, and environment 
(‘SHE’), and manufacturing. The Company’s internal 
audit activity is managed through the Management 
Assurance Services (‘MAS’) function. It is an 
important element of the overall process by which 
the Audit Committee and the Board obtains 
assurance on the effectiveness of internal controls 
over financial reporting.
The scope of work including annual internal audit 
plan, authority, and resources of MAS are regularly 
reviewed and approved by the Audit Committee. 
Annual internal audit plan is aligned with ERM to 
ensure that all critical risks are covered in the audit 
plan. Besides, its work is supported by the services 
of leading international audit firms. The annual 
internal audit includes: monthly physical 
verification of inventory and review of accounts/ 
MIS and a quarterly review of critical business 
processes. To enhance internal controls, the 
internal audit follows a stringent grading 
mechanism, monitoring and reporting of the 
implementation of internal auditors’ 
recommendations of internal audit. The internal 
auditors make periodic presentations on audit 
observations, including the status of follow-up to 
the Audit Committee.
During the year under review, neither the Statutory 
Auditors nor the Secretarial Auditor has reported 
to the Audit Committee, under Section 143(12) of 
the Companies Act, 2013, any instances of fraud 
committed against the Company by its officers or 
employees, the details of which would need to be 
mentioned in the Boards' report.

OFC Rakholi Plant:In FY26, various initiatives are taken up across our 
plants which has contributed to a decrease in 
energy consumption and hence the carbon 
footprint. 
a.Roof top green solar installation under Phase-2 
of solar installation with new roof sheet along 
with the skylight at day time to reduce the 
plant lighting load lights of total 38kw yearly 
saving 2040266 units. Total Solar Capacity 
installed in All Cables plant in India is ~1,623.78 
KWp.
b.Installed Water flow meters in bore-wells, 
Water level sensors in tanks.
c.Cooling tower running optimization through 
centralized system and along with fan control 
through temp sensor to reduce the power 
consumption of running cooling tower with 
6,570 kl of water saving through evaporation 
losses.
d.Installed a parallel UPS system with 
power-saving mode,
e.Modified the chiller pipeline to run a single 
chiller for the entire plant.
f.Optimized the new FG line pipeline and 
decommissioned one pump.
g.Modified the buff line pipeline and 
decommissioned one pump, saving 4.22 lakhs 
per year.Glass Shendra Plants:
a.Lighting Optimization: Timer-based controls 
implemented in passage areas (RIC/Canteen), 
reducing electricity consumption.
b.VFD Frequency Optimization: Fine-tuned 
Scrubber (A/B/C) and Cooling Tower pump 
performance to reduce energy consumption by 
125,000 units annually.
OFC Rakholi Plant:
a.Release of grid connectivity to 1623.79 Kwp 
Solar Ground/ Rooftop Mounted power plant 
resulting in total Solar Unit generation of 
2040266 unit.
b.Exploring the source of power injection 
through open access. Additionally, the 
Company has observed significant benefits 
from using solar power during DG runtime, 
which has resulted in reduced diesel costs.
OF Shendra Plant:
a.Sub-Potable Water Reclamation: Utilized 
treated effluent from STPs for landscaping, 
minimizing primary freshwater dependency.
b.Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) Infrastructure: 
Leveraged a 40 KLD ETP to facilitate a 
closed-loop hydraulic system, enabling 
high-grade process water recovery.
c.Advanced Evaporative Recovery: Optimized 
40 KLD MEE plants to drive thermal separation 
and maximize distillate recovery through 
precision evaporation and condensation cycles.OFC Waluj Plant:
a.Expansion of existing plant with revised layout, 
which helps to increase production without 
significant changes in Power demand.
b.In-house development for IBR loose tube in 
existing Buffering line with single Pay Off to 
get 10% energy saving with same fibre count 
normal loose tube.
SCB Dadra plant:
a.Installing a new auxiliary compressor for the 
nitrogen plant allows the main compressor to 
run at a lower pressure.
b.Replacing the CP reciprocating compressor 
with a 600 CFM VFD screw compressor.
c.Converting all filler line and two sheathing lines 
from DC systems to AC will increase annual 
energy savings.OF Shendra Plant:
a.Power Factor Optimization: Integrated Auto-
mated Power Factor Correction (APFC) 
capacitor banks in the Phase-2 Furnace SDB 
Panel. This improved the Power Factor (PF) 
significantly reducing kVA demand charges.
b.Mitigation of Harmonic Distortion: Installed 
Active Harmonic Filters (AHF) on Phase-1 SDB 
Panels to reduce Total Harmonic Distortion 
(THD) from levels of 18-25% to below 8%. This 
initiative minimises energy losses caused by 
harmonics and is expected to yield a 2-3% 
reduction in overall energy consumption.
c.Introduced hybrid (UV+LED) systems in two 
towers, resulting in a reduction of energy 
consumption.
d.Upgrading induction furnaces from SCR-based 
switching to IGBT-based controlling to 
minimise switching losses and enhance thermal 
efficiency.

PHILOSOPHY OF THE COMPANY ON CODE OF GOVERNANCE 
OF GOVERNANCE
Composition of BoardBOARD OF DIRECTORSStrategic supervision
Strategic management
Executive managementEffective corporate governance practices constitute 
the strong foundation on which successful 
commercial enterprises are built to last. Corporate 
Governance represents the values, ethical and moral 
framework under which business decisions are 
taken. The investors want to be sure that not only is 
their capital handled effectively and adds to the 
creation of wealth, but the business decisions are 
also taken in a manner which is not illegal or 
involves moral hazard. 
Our Company perceives good corporate 
governance practices as key to sustainable 
corporate growth and long-term shareholder value 
The Board of Directors occupies the topmost tier in the governance structure. It plays a role of 
strategic supervision that is devoid of involvement in the task of strategic management of the 
Company. The Board lays down strategic goals and exercises control to ensure that the 
Company is progressing to fulfil stakeholders’ aspirations.
The Executive Committee consists of the Company's senior management and functions under 
the supervision and direction of the Board of Directors.
The function of Management Committee is to execute and realise the goals that are laid down 
by the Board and the Executive Committee.
The Company’s Board comprises directors from 
diverse backgrounds and substantial experience, who 
are able to provide appropriate guidance to the 
executive management as required. As on March 31, 
2026, the Board of Directors of the Company (‘the 
Board’) comprises Eight Directors of which three are 
Whole-time Directors and five are Non-Executive 
Directors including one Independent Woman 
director. Mr. Anil Agarwal is a Non-Executive 
Chairman and Mr. Pravin Agarwal is the Vice 
Chairman of the Board. The Board has no institutional 
nominee Director. The Board composition is in 
compliance with the requirements of Regulation 17 of 
SEBI Listing Regulations, requiring not less than half 
the Board to be Independent. The profiles of 
Directors are available at 
https://stl.tech/management/?_management_filter=
board-of-directors
All Directors have made necessary disclosures 
regarding Directorships and Committee positions held 
by them in other companies. None of the Directors 
holds directorships in more than ten public 
companies. None of them is a Member of more than 
ten Committees and Chairman of more than five 
Committees across all companies in which he/ she is a 
Director. None of the Company’s Independent 
Directors serves as an Independent Director in more 
than seven listed companies. For the purpose of 
determination of limit of the Board Committees, 
chairpersonship and membership of the Audit 
Committee and Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee 
has been considered as per Regulation 26(1)(b) of 
SEBI Listing Regulations. All Non-Independent 
Directors on the Board are liable to retire by rotation. 
The appointment of the Whole-time Directors, 
including their tenure and remuneration is also approved by the Board.
Mr. Pravin Agarwal, Mr. Ankit Agarwal and Mr. Venkatesh 
Murthy, Whole-time Directors of the Company, are not 
appointed as Independent Directors of any Listed 
Company. 
Independent Directors are non-executive directors as 
defined under Regulation 16(1)(b) of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations and Section 149(6) of the Companies Act, 
2013 (‘Act’) along with rules framed thereunder. In terms of 
Regulation 25(8) of SEBI Listing Regulations, they have 
confirmed that they are not aware of any circumstance or 
situation which exists or may be reasonably anticipated 
that could impair or impact their ability to discharge their 
duties. Based on the declarations received from the 
Independent Directors, the Board of Directors has 
confirmed that they meet the criteria of independence as 
mentioned under Section 149(6) of the Act and Regulation 
16(1)(b) of the SEBI Listing Regulations and that they are 
independent of the management. The Company does not 
have any pecuniary relationship with any of the 
non-executive directors. Further, during the year, the 
Company has not provided any loans or advances to 
firms/companies in which directors are interested.
Pursuant to Regulation 27(2) of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations, the Company also submits a quarterly 
compliance report on Corporate Governance to the Indian 
Stock Exchanges, including details on all material 
transactions with related parties, within statutory timelines. 
The Managing Director and the Chief Financial Officer 
(‘CFO’) have certified to the Board on, inter alia, the creation. The primary objective is to develop and 
adhere to a corporate culture of harmonious and 
transparent functioning, increasing employee and client 
satisfaction and enhancing shareholders’ wealth by 
developing capabilities and identifying opportunities 
that best serve the goal of value creation.

Schedule V and sub-regulation (2) of Regulation 46 of 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), as applicable, with

II.   AUDIT COMMITTEE A. Auditors
B.  Internal Audit & Internal Controls
C. Gover nanceThe Audit Committee of the Board is governed by a 
Charter drawn in accordance with the requirements 
of the Act and Regulation 18 of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations and Section 177 of the Act, besides 
other terms as may be referred to by the Board of 
Directors. The primary objective of the Audit 
Committee of the Board of Directors is to discharge 
responsibilities relating to accounting and reporting 
of financial practices adopted by the Company and 
its subsidiaries, surveillance of internal financial 
control systems as well as accounting and audit 
activities. 
The Audit Committee comprises of four 
Independent Directors. The Chairman of the 
Committee (Independent Director) is a Chartered 
Accountant and has accounting and financial 
expertise. The other Committee members also are 
financially literate. The quorum of the Committee is 
two members or one-third of its members, 
whichever is higher with at least two Independent 
Directors. 
Audit Committee meetings are usually attended by 
the Executive Directors, the CFO and 
representatives of Statutory Auditors and Internal 
Auditors. Business CEOs and Functional Heads are 
also invited to the meetings, as and when needed. 
The Company Secretary acts as the Secretary to 
Audit Committee. The Internal Audit function 
reports to the Audit Committee to ensure its 
The terms of reference of the Audit Committee 
includes: 
1.Reviewing the Company’s financial reporting 
processes and the disclosure of its financial 
information to ensure the financial statements 
are correct, sufficient and credible.
2.Reviewing with the management, the quarterly 
and annual financial statements and the 
Auditors’ report before submission to the Board 
for approval, focusing primarily on:
i.Matters required to be included in the 
Directors' Responsibility Statement being 
part of the Annual Board Report;
ii.Compliance with accounting standards and 
changes in accounting policies and 
practices and the reasons for the same;
iii.Major accounting entries involving estimates 
based on exercise of judgment by 
Management;
iv.Audit qualifications and significant 
adjustments in the financial statements, 
arising out of the audit;
v.Compliance with listing and other legal 
requirements relating to financial 
statements.
vi.Disclosure of any related party transactions;
vii.Modified Opinion(s) in the Statutory 
Auditors Report, if any; as well as reviewing 
the Auditors Report for the Key Audit 
Matters, if any; Contingent liabilities; 
viii.Status of litigations by or against the 
Company; and
ix.Claims against the Company and their effect 1.Recommending the appointment, terms of 
appointment and removal of auditors and the 
fixation of audit fees, including, payment to 
Statutory Auditors for any other services 
rendered and any other related payments.
2.Reviewing the Statutory Auditor’s independence 
and performance and scrutinizing the 
effectiveness of the entire audit process.
3.Discussing with the Statutory Auditors the 
nature and scope of their audit as well as having 
post-audit discussions.
4.Reviewing management letters/ letters of 
internal control weaknesses issued by the 
Statutory Auditors.
5.Recommending the appointment of secretarial 
and cost auditors along with their fees and 
reviewing their periodic audit reports.
1.Reviewing with the management the 
performance and adequacy of the Internal Audit 
function, the structure of the Internal Audit 
department, the adequacy of the staffing of the 
department, the reporting structure, coverage 
and frequency of the Internal Audit and the 
significant findings and follow-up there on.
2.Reviewing with the Internal Auditors, the plans 
for and the scope of their ongoing audit 
activities and also review and approve the 
periodicity and programme for conducting the 
internal audit.
3.Reviewing the Internal Auditors’ independence, 
performance and scrutinizing the effectiveness 
of the entire Audit process.
4.Reviewing the findings of any internal 
investigations by the Internal Auditors into 
matters where there is suspected fraud or 
irregularity or a failure of internal control 
systems of a material nature and reporting the 
matter to the Board.
5.Reviewing the internal financial control 
framework and Risk Management systems.
6.Reviewing internal audit reports relating to 
internal control weaknesses.
7.Approving appointment, removal and terms of 
remuneration of the Chief Internal Auditor.
Reviewing, with the management, the statement of

Approving any transactions or subsequent modifica-

c.As a result of its businesses and the global 
nature of its operations, the Company is 
exposed in particular to market risks from 
changes in foreign currency exchange rates 
and interest rates, while commodity price risks 
arise from procurement. The Company has 
established internal guidelines for risk 
controlling procedures and for the use of 
financial instruments, including a clear 
segregation of duties with regard to financial 
activities, settlement, accounting and the 
related controlling. The guidelines upon which 
the Company’s risk management processes for 
financial risks are based, are designed to 
identify and analyze these risks throughout the 
company, to set appropriate risk limits and 
controls and to monitor the risks by means of 
reliable and up-to-date administrative and 
information systems. The guidelines and 
systems are regularly reviewed and adjusted to 
changes in markets and products. The 
Company enters into forward contracts for 
hedging foreign exchange exposures against 
exports and imports.

The Board has also constituted the Authorization 
and Allotment Committee, to assist in discharging 
its functions. This Committee operates within the

Directors.
The Board of Directors of the Company is 
committed to assessing its own performance as a 
Board in order to identify its strengths and areas in 
which it may improve its functioning. To that end, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee has 
established processes for performance evaluation 
of Independent Directors, the Board and 
Committees of the Board.
Pursuant to the provisions of the Act, and the SEBI 
Listing Regulations, the Board has carried out an

directors individually. A structured evaluation was 
carried out based on various parameters such as 
skills and experience to perform the role, level of 
participation, contribution to strategy, degree of 
oversight, professional conduct and independence.
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee 
(‘NRC’) has adopted a Charter which, inter alia, 
deals with the manner of selection of the Directors,

accordingly derived from the said Charter.
The NRC shall identify and ascertain the

appointment.
The Term of the Directors including Managing

Whereas the term of the KMP (other than the

WHISTLEBLOWER MECHANISM
The Company has adopted a Whistleblower 
Mechanism, which has been communicated to all 
employees along with Code of Business Conduct & 
Ethics. The Whistleblower policy is the mechanism 
to help the Company’s directors, employees, its 
subsidiaries and all external stakeholders to raise 
their concerns about any malpractice, impropriety, 
abuse or wrongdoing at an early stage and in the 
right way, without fear of victimization, subsequent 
discrimination or disadvantage. The policy 
encourages raising concerns within the Company 
rather than overlooking a problem. All Complaints 
under this policy are reported to the Director - 
Management Assurance, who is independent of 
operating management and businesses. 
‘Complaints’ can also be reported on a web-based 
portal, designated email id or toll-free number as

been extended to external stakeholders like

DISCLOSURES
a.The Company has complied with the

relating to capital markets. No penalties or

the SEBI or any statutory authorities on any 
matter relating to the above. As per Regulation 
23(9) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, every 
listed entity has to submit to the Stock 
Exchanges, disclosures of related party 
transactions every six months on the date of

(“NSE”) vide communication dated June 27,

has made the waiver application with the NSE

the Company has been granted an exemption 
from payment of fine imposed.
b.The Company has not received any complaints 
relating to child labour, forced labour, 
involuntary labour during FY 2026.
c.As a result of its businesses and the global 
nature of its operations, the Company is 
exposed in particular to market risks from 
changes in foreign currency exchange rates 
and interest rates, while commodity price risks 
arise from procurement. The Company has 
established internal guidelines for risk 
controlling procedures and for the use of 
financial instruments, including a clear 
segregation of duties with regard to financial 
activities, settlement, accounting and the 
related controlling. The guidelines upon which 
the Company’s risk management processes for 
financial risks are based, are designed to 
identify and analyze these risks throughout the 
company, to set appropriate risk limits and 
controls and to monitor the risks by means of 
reliable and up-to-date administrative and 
information systems. The guidelines and 
systems are regularly reviewed and adjusted to 
changes in markets and products. The

Share Transfer System
DISPUTE RESOLUTION MECHANISM
Sterlite Technologies Limit edIn terms of Regulation 40(1) of SEBI Listing 
Regulations, as amended from time to time, 
transfer, transmission and transposition of 
securities shall be effected only in dematerialized 
form.
Pursuant to SEBI Circular dated January 25, 2022, 
the listed companies shall issue the securities in 
dematerialized form only, for processing any 
service requests from shareholders viz., issue of 
duplicate share certificates, endorsement, 
transmission, transposition, etc. After processing 
the service request, a letter of confirmation will be 
issued to the shareholders and shall be valid for a 
period of 120 days, within which the shareholder 
shall make a request to the Depository Participant 
for dematerialising those shares. If the 
shareholders fail to submit the dematerialisation 
request within 120 days, then the Company shall 
credit those shares in the Suspense Escrow Demat 
account held by the Company. Shareholders can 
claim these shares transferred to Suspense 
Escrow Demat account on submission of 
necessary documentation.
Pursuant to the SEBI circular no. 
HO/38/13/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/ I/3750/2026 
dated January 30, 2026. The Company has 
opened a special window for re-lodgment of 
transfer requests of physical shares from July 07, 
2025 to February 04, 2026 to enable the physical 
shareholders to re-lodge request(s) to transfer 
their physical shares including those requests that 
are pending with the listed Company/Registrar 
and Transfer Agent prior to April 1, 2019. SEBI has vide its Circular No. 
SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/76 
dated May 30, 2022, issued a Standard Operating 
Procedure (‘SOP’) for dispute resolution under the 
Stock Exchange Arbitration Mechanism for 
disputes between a listed company and/or 
registrars to an issue and share transfer agents 
and its shareholder(s)/investor(s).
The Company has complied with the same and is 
accessible on the website of the Company. 
SCORES: A centralised web based complaints 
redress system ‘SCORES’ which serves as a 
centralised database of all complaints received, 
enables uploading of Action Taken Reports by the 
concerned companies and online viewing by the 
investors of actions taken on complaints and its 
current status.
ONLINE DISPUTE RESOLUTION 
PORTAL (‘ODR PORTAL’):
A mechanism to streamline and strengthen the 
existing dispute resolution in the Indian Securities 
Market, SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OI-
AE_IAD-3/P/CIR/2023/195 dated July 31, 2023 
(updated as on December 20, 2023), introduced 
the ODR Portal. This mechanism enhanced the 
degree of regulatory supervision by SEBI over 
disputes between aggrieved parties and the ODR 
order is binding on both the parties to the dispute. 
Pursuant to above-mentioned circulars, the 
aggrieved party can initiate the mechanism 
through the ODR portal, after exercising the 
primary options to resolve the issue directly with 
the Company and through the SCORES platform.Sterlite Technologies Limited Suspense Escrow 
Demat Account
In accordance with the requirements of SEBI 
Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/ 
CIR/2022/8 dated January 25, 2022 the Company 
has opened a Suspense Escrow Demat Account 
with the Depository Participant for transfer of 
shares lying unclaimed for more than 120 days 
from the date of issue of Letter of Confirmation 
(‘LOC’) to the shareholders in lieu of physical 
share certificate(s) to enable them to make a 
request to Depository Participant (‘DP’) for 
dematerialising their shares.
During the year under review, 3920 shares 
pertaining to 12 shareholders were transferred to 
the Company’s Suspense Escrow Demat Account. 
Further, 3 requests were received from sharehold-
ers for release of 815 shares from the said 
suspense escrow demat account of the Company 
and the same were released accordingly.
All the corporate benefits against these shares like 
bonus shares, split, etc., would also be transferred 
to Suspense Escrow Demat Account of the 
Company. While the dividend for the shares which 
are lying in Suspense Escrow Demat Account 
would be credited back to the relevant dividend 
accounts of the Company.The voting rights on shares lying in Suspense 
Escrow Demat Account shall remain frozen till the 
rightful owner claims the shares.

be issued on and after April 2, 2026 and instead, 
securities will now be credited directly to the 
investor's demat account. However, any LOC 
issued before April 2, 2026, may be submitted by 
the investors to DP for dematerialisation within 
the specified timeline i.e.  120 days from the date

identify and analyze these risks throughout the

controls and to monitor the risks by means of 
reliable and up-to-date administrative and 
information systems. The guidelines and 
systems are regularly reviewed and adjusted to 
changes in markets and products. The

18FY25Details of improvements in
environmental and social impact
A) OFNR rated Cable (Microdistrubution cable and Higher 
fiber count cable) - It provides a significant step up in safety 
and reliability for vertical building infrastructure. 
(Low Smoke Zero Halogen qualified)
1. Flame Retardancy: OFNR cables are treated with fire-
retardant chemicals to prevent fire from traveling between 
floors via riser shafts
2. Resource Efficiency: Because OFNR is designed specifically 
for vertical runs, it allows for more efficient cable routing in 
high-rise buildings
3. Longevity: These cables are built to be robust. A longer 
lifecycle means fewer replacements, leading to less electronic 
waste (e-waste) and a lower long-term carbon footprint for 
building maintenance.
4. Life Safety in High-Rises: The "Riser" rating is a legal safety 
requirement. In the event of a fire, OFNR cables are designed 
to self-extinguish and prevent the "chimney effect" (where 
fire spreads rapidly upward through shafts). This directly 
protects the lives of residents and office workers.
Compliance and Ethics: Using OFNR ensures that developers 
are meeting building codes. Socially, this represents a 
commitment to ethical construction standards and occupant 
well-being over "cutting corners" with cheaper, flammable 
materials.22.77%
56.61% CapexB) Microdistrubution cable - 
1. Material Reduction: Micro distribution cables are designed 
with a smaller diameter and higher fiber density. This 
reduces the amount of raw materials—such as plastics for 
buffering and aramid yarns for strength—needed per fiber 
kilometer.
2. Lower Carbon Footprint in Logistics: Because the cables 
are thinner and lighter, more cable can be wound onto a 
single reel. This reduces the number of shipments required 
and lowers the transportation-related CO2 emissions.
C) G.654.E are centered on energy efficiency and infrastru-
cture optimization
1. Significant Energy Savings: Because G.654.E has much 
lower signal attenuation, light can travel much further before 
it needs to be "re-amplified." By reducing the number of 
optical amplifiers and repeaters required along a thousand-
mile route, the total power consumption of the network is 
significantly lowered.
2. Material Efficiency: By supporting higher bandwidth 
(like 800G) over a single fiber pair, G.654.E allows providers 
to increase network capacity without laying new physical 0.00%02

standards that govern our global operations. We believe that true integrity is a collective responsibility; 
therefore, we rely on the shared commitment of our employees and stakeholders to uphold our core 
values. Every member of our workforce is expected to strictly adhere to our Code of Business Conduct 
and Ethics, ensuring these principles are integrated into every level of our organization.
To maintain a transparent and accountable environment, we have established a robust Whistle-blower 
Policy. This framework empowers internal staff, off-roll workers, and external partners including 
vendors and customers to report concerns regarding malpractice or misconduct at an early stage. 
We guarantee protection against reprisal, ensuring all voices are heard through our dedicated toll-free 
helplines and email channels displayed across all offices.
Furthermore, we are committed to providing a safe, respectful workplace. This is overseen by our 
Prevention of Sexual Harassment Committee (PSHC), which manages complaints with the utmost 
confidentiality and effectiveness. To reinforce this, we conduct mandatory annual training sessions to

10.Health and safety management system:
a. Whether an occupational health and safety 
management system has been implemented 
by the entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the 
coverage such system?
b. What are the processes used to identify 
work-related hazards and assess risks on 
a routine and non-routine basis by the 
entity?
c. Whether you have processes for workers to 
report the work-related hazards and to remove 
themselves from such risks. (Yes/No)
d. Do the employees/ worker of the entity have 
access to non-occupational medical and 
healthcare services? (Yes/No)As an ISO 45001-certified organization, we 
protect the safety and well-being of our 
workforce through rigorous risk assessment 
and management. Using our internal tools, we 
systematically evaluate process risks on both 
a routine and non-routine basis, allowing us to 
proactively identify and mitigate potential 
hazards.
Our dedication to environmental and safety 
excellence is anchored in our comprehensive 
Quality, Environment, Health, and Safety 
(QEHS) policy, which governs all manufactur -
ing processes. Every operational area is 
strictly monitored under ISO 14001 (Environ -
mental Management Systems) and ISO 45001 
(Occupational Health and Safety) frameworks. 
This structured monitoring ensures we contin -
uously improve our workflows and quickly 
address any operational gaps.To maintain high safety awareness, our entire 
workforce has full access to our QEHS policy 
and Hazard Identification and Risk Assess -
ment (HIRA) procedures. Clear Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs) are readily 
available to guide workers through potential 
risks, actively preventing on-duty injuries and 
illnesses.
If a work-related incident occurs, we immedi -
ately activate robust accident investigation 
procedures to analyze the root cause and 
prevent recurrence. Furthermore, our plant 
implementation committees spearhead vital 
safety initiatives such as Project Abhay- to 
drive cultural transformation in our EHS 
practices and continually optimize our safety 
protocols.
To systematically identify work-related 
hazards and evaluate risks, we rely on the 
following core processes and SOPs:
•Comprehensive Hazard Assessment: We 
identify occupational safety hazards and 
risks across all activities, making adher -
ence to control measures mandatory. Any 
non-routine or high-risk task strictly 
requires an authorized Permit to Work 
(PTW) before execution.
•Routine & Non-Routine HIRA: We regular -
ly perform hazard identification and risk 
assessments across all daily and occasion -
al operations.
•Rigorous Incident Investigation: We 
thoroughly investigate every work-related 
incident using established procedures, 
using the insights to implement preventa -
tive actions and drive continuous 
improvement.

     suitable employmentEmployees Yes
Workers YesLeadership IndicatorsProactive Risk Mitigation and Safety Tools
To identify risks before they manifest, we systemati -
cally utilize advanced risk-assessment methodolo -
gies, including:
•HIRA (Hazard Identification and Risk Assess -
ment)
•HAZOP (Hazard and Operability Study)
•PSSR (Pre-Startup Safety Review)
•MOC (Management of Change)
When mitigating identified risks, we strictly follow 
the industry-standard Hierarchy of Controls, priori -
tizing solutions in the following order: Elimination, 
Substitution, Engineering Controls, Administrative 
Controls, and lastly, Personal Protective Equipment 
(PPE).
Workforce Empowerment and Continuous Learning
We actively build a strong safety culture by granting 
our employees full access to HIRA, HAZOP, and 
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). These 
resources empower our workforce with the vital 
knowledge required to identify hazards, evaluate 
risks, and protect themselves from injury or illness 
on the job.
If a work-related incident does occur, we launch an 
exhaustive investigation through established proto -
cols. This ensures we extract valuable insights from 
every event, continuously strengthening our safety 
protocols and workplace standards.Incident Management and CAPA (Project Abhay)
Under our flagship initiative, Project Abhay, we 
maintain a dedicated Incident Management (IM) 
vertical. This specialized division thoroughly investi -
gates every potential incident to determine its root 
cause, establish definitive Corrective and Preventive 
Actions (CAPA), and verify the long-term effective -
ness of those actions.
The primary goal of this framework is to prevent any 
recurrence. Overseeing this process is our Incident 
Management Subcommittee, a cross-functional 
body responsible for delivering unbiased, high-quali -
ty investigations and horizontally deploying key 
safety findings across all relevant company 
locations.

8.  Does the entity have any project related to reducing Green House Gas emission? If yes, then provide 
     details.
Yes, our company is dedicated to optimizing operations and enhancing efficiency through several strategic 
initiatives:
Implemented energy optimization in the PH-2 building’s third-floor cleanroom by reconfiguring the layout 
with localized partitioning around tower. This spatial reduction enabled the deactivation of the associated 
Air Handling Unit (AHU), resulting in an energy savings of approximately 15 lakh units per year.
Replaced UV lamp systems in two towers with UV LED, resulting in a reduction of energy consumption by 
approximately 11 lakh units per year.
 
Optimized the cooling system for the P1 and P2 UPS rooms by modifying the AHU ducting layout to improve 
airflow efficiency and thermal distribution. This modification aligns cooling capacity with actual thermal load, 
yielding an estimated energy savings of 1.4 lakh units per year on a seasonal basis.
Implemented energy savings by converting lightly loaded motors (operating below 50% load) from delta to 
star connection on a permanent basis. This modification reduced voltage and current draw, leading to 
improved power factor and an energy savings of approximately 95,040 units per year.
 
Installed Variable Frequency Drives(VFDs) on PH-1 primary pump motors to enable load-based speed 
regulation, optimizing pump performance and reducing energy consumption. This implementation has 
resulted in an estimated energy savings of 96,000 units per year.
Integrating Proof Testing and Coloring processes optimizing power consumption by streamlining operations 
and enabling more efficient resource utilization. By combining these processes, we minimized equipment needs, 
decrease downtime, and improve overall energy balance. This implementation in five machines has resulted in 
an estimated energy savings of 2.2 lakh units per year.
These initiatives underscore our commitment to sustainable practices and continuous improvement, 
contributing to both environmental stewardship and operational excellence.

     What mitigation or adaptation measures have been taken by the entity in this regard.Assessing both acute and chronic climate-related risks to our physical and operational assets is a core 
element of our business continuity and disaster management frameworks. Our comprehensive risk 
evaluations cover localized vulnerabilities—such as water scarcity, extreme temperature fluctuations, 
structural fires, and natural disasters—as well as macro-level disruptions, including regional or national 
pandemic outbreaks.
To manage these threats effectively, we operate a robust business continuity program focused on 
continuous monitoring and proactive mitigation. By embedding preventative strategies and structured 
contingency protocols into our operations, we safeguard our business against disruptions and ensure the 
unbroken resilience of our value chain, even when confronted with severe climate-driven events.

The carrying amount of investments in equity 
shares of Sterlite Global Ventures (Mauritius) 
Limited and Sterlite (Shanghai) Trading Compa -
ny Limited as of March 31, 2026, aggregated to 
/uni20B9262 crore and the loans to STL Digital Limited 
and Sterlite Technologies Holding Inc USA as at 
March 31, 2026, aggregated to /uni20B9390 crore. 
Further, the Company has also given guarantees 
in respect of external borrowings taken by these 
subsidiaries. 
The Company accounts for investments in 
subsidiaries at cost (less accumulated impair-
ment, if any). The management reviews the 
carrying value of these investments in subsidiar-
ies at each reporting date and assesses if there 
are any indicators of impairment. 
The Management has used the discounted cash 
flow (‘DCF’) model for estimating the recover-
able amount of the investments for the purpose 
of carrying out the impairment assessment, 
which involves estimates and judgement with 
regard to certain key inputs like future cashflows, 
discount rates, terminal growth rate, economic 
factors, etc. incorporated in the valuation.
Further, in respect of the aforementioned loans 
and guarantees, the Company applies the princi-
ples of Ind AS 109 “Financial Instruments” to 
determine whether any provision for expected 
credit losses (‘ECL’) is required, considering the 
expected manner of recovery over a period and 
other variables considered in the ECL model. 
We considered this to be a key audit matter due 
to significant management judgement involved in 
estimating of the recoverable amount.
